headline: Coupling spatial transcriptomics with histology and graph structure to infer domains
label: Spatial Transcriptomics Computational Inference
summary: Recent preprints and published tools fuse spatial graphs, histology, and foundation-model pretraining with expression to resolve spatial domains and niches.
synthesis: The dominant thread is conditioning spatial transcriptomic expression inference on neighborhood graph structure, histology, or other modalities rather than analysing spots or cells independently. MultiST fuses spatial graph, expression, and histology via cross-attention to refine domain boundaries across 13 datasets, and AugGCL combines expression with image morphology to decode spatial domains. HARMONIC uses histology-aware graphs to infer spatially contextualized cell-cell communication, and COSMIC links nuclear morphology with gene expression using paired image-transcriptome data. SAGE-FM applies a lightweight GCN foundation model trained on 416 Visium samples with interpretable masked-gene recovery. Other items extend the logic to scale or statistics: SparseAEH uses block-wise sparse Gaussian kernels for dense data, and SpaceBF estimates local and global spatial co-expression under Bayesian fused priors. What is new is explicit spatial or morphological conditioning of expression inference, applied to larger datasets and across modalities, including spatial metabolomics in MANTIS and virtual staining in miniMTI.
